IR.rationale: Bond futures are a large part of trend-follower risk, and the sleeve has typically been long duration. A rise in intermediate yields relative to policy marks a bond sell-off that hurts those positions until signals turn.

B.rationale: Persistently widening credit spreads mark a risk-off state. In such states trend followers tend to accumulate profitable short-risk and long-safe-asset positions.

V.rationale: Time-series momentum returns are larger when markets are volatile and trending. Elevated equity volatility proxies for that environment.

AP.rationale: A joint developed and emerging equity decline is the broad risk-off trend in which managed futures show their documented crisis-alpha, straddle-like payoff.

ST.rationale: Cross-sectional equity momentum shares a common trend-persistence component with time-series momentum across asset classes.

FX.rationale: Broad dollar moves are among the most persistent trends that CTA currency books capture.

COM.rationale: Broad commodity moves tend to persist and feed directly into CTA commodity sleeves.

MC.rationale: High financial stress is associated with sustained deleveraging trends across asset classes, which favour trend followers.

ENDG.rationale: Trend-following returns show some persistence because the market trends they exploit are themselves persistent.

IR.rationale: Bond sell-offs against long-duration trend positions generate abrupt losses and so raise CTA return variance.

B.rationale: Credit spread widening signals a turbulent cross-asset regime with larger moves in the futures that CTAs hold.

V.rationale: Diversified CTA risk depends on volatility across asset classes. Equity and oil implied volatility jointly high is a broad high-volatility state.

AP.rationale: Equity declines raise volatility through the leverage and risk-aversion channels, and this spills over to CTA positions.

ST.rationale: Weak momentum signals trend reversals and momentum-crash conditions. Under these conditions trend-following P&L becomes more volatile.

FX.rationale: Yen appreciation marks carry unwinds and risk-off shocks, which produce sharp cross-asset moves.

COM.rationale: Commodity sell-offs tend to come with higher commodity and macro volatility.

MC.rationale: Financial stress is a well-documented predictor of elevated volatility across markets.

ENDG.rationale: High recent realised variance carries volatility-clustering information beyond the baseline.

IR.rationale: A sharp back-up in yields is the classic reversal that hits CTAs' long-bond trend positions.

B.rationale: Credit stress states raise the risk of whipsaw and abrupt policy-driven reversals.

V.rationale: High-volatility regimes raise the probability of sharp trend reversals and therefore tail losses.

AP.rationale: Strong equity rebounds after declines catch trend followers positioned short risk, mirroring the documented momentum-crash pattern.

ST.rationale: Momentum losing while short-term reversal pays is a reversal-dominated regime, which is hostile to trend strategies.

FX.rationale: Sudden yen rallies reflect abrupt carry and risk unwinds that reverse established FX trends.

COM.rationale: Sharp commodity rebounds reverse the persistent commodity trends CTAs ride, especially after declines.

MC.rationale: Stress regimes coincide with policy interventions that can trigger violent reversals.

ENDG.rationale: After extended strong runs, positions are crowded and trend-reversal tail risk rises.

IR.rationale: Falling short and intermediate yields together describe an easing or flight-to-quality bond rally that rewards long-bond trends.

B.rationale: Widening spreads with falling high-yield prices describe a building credit-stress trend in which managed futures earn crisis alpha.

V.rationale: High market and policy uncertainty together accompany the large sustained macro moves that produce CTA tail gains.

AP.rationale: A global equity sell-off is the setting of the documented convex, straddle-like payoff of trend followers.

ST.rationale: Strong momentum performance signals a trend-persistent environment that favours large CTA gains.

FX.rationale: Strong dollar trends, often safe-haven driven, are a major source of large CTA currency gains.

COM.rationale: Persistent commodity sell-offs have been a significant source of outsized trend-follower gains through short positions.

MC.rationale: Rising financial stress drives the prolonged cross-asset deleveraging trends behind CTA tail gains.

ENDG.rationale: Strong recent performance indicates an established trend regime that can extend into further large gains.
